lighthouse-basement.title: Lighthouse hidden basement: levers and opening conditions
lighthouse-basement.html:
The yellow lever is assigned to the hidden basement. Try interacting with it first; pulling it alone is not yet confirmed to open the doors.

The three levers

Blue: lighthouse. Green: furnace. Yellow: basement. Both lighthouse variants use this mapping.

What if the lighthouse is not ready?

The game includes a lighthouse-not-ready message. It is not yet clear whether this requires waiting or operating other levers. The blue → green → yellow order has not been verified.

Confirmed basement configuration

The basement’s facilities include four runes, four doors, four flames, loot spawn points and a radiation area. Rune lighting and flames going out involve timers, but their starting points, resets and role in opening the doors are unknown.

Still unverified

The full lever sequence, required lit runes, waiting time, door-open duration and radiation conditions remain unconfirmed. The available evidence is insufficient for guaranteed opening instructions.

military-base-keycard.title: Military base keycard: how to obtain it
military-base-keycard.html:
Visit the military base (Citadel), defeat its guards and check their dropped loot. A keycard may drop; it cannot be crafted.

Local resources link the easy, medium and hard guard loot tables to the military base keycard. A successful selection of this loot entry produces one card. A kill does not guarantee a drop.

The tables also use selection and quantity rules. The final drop rate is unconfirmed, and no guard tier can yet be declared the best source.

According to the official guide, use the card at the access terminal on the roof of the central radar building. It is consumed to call an airdrop, notifying nearby players. The radar then enters a cooldown.

plane-crash-keycard.title: Plane crash keycard: acquisition clues and open questions
plane-crash-keycard.html:
The relevant item is the Captain Keycard. It cannot be crafted and appears in a plane-specific loot table. The exact container and pickup location remain unconfirmed.

Confirmed clues

The Captain Keycard is included among plane-related loot, with one card awarded when it appears. The actual container is still unknown; not every plane crate is confirmed to contain one.

Where should you look?

The available clues point to loot boxes associated with keys and tools around the crash site. The exact box, location and route have not been confirmed.

Where is the card used?

There is a card reader at the crash site. The card’s description explicitly says it does not work inside the cockpit. The correct reader and the door it opens still need verification.

Still unconfirmed

The actual container, location, respawn conditions, drop rate and door-opening steps need further investigation or in-game verification. A guaranteed route to obtain the card is not yet available.

avoid-animal-attacks.title: How to avoid animal attacks
avoid-animal-attacks.html:
When a bear, boar or wolf chases you in the wilderness, use higher ground to create distance and find an opportunity to fight back.

Look for something you can jump onto

Quickly look for a raised platform, barrel, car or building foundation you can reach. Choose a spot the animal has difficulty reaching. Once up, check that you are no longer taking damage and stay away from the edge; low platforms or positions too close to the animal may still be unsafe.

Fight back with a ranged weapon

Once your position is safe, use a bow, crossbow or firearm to attack the animal below. Bring the matching arrows, bolts or ammunition, and avoid moving toward the edge to take a shot.

Build a foundation if there is no suitable cover

If there is nowhere suitable to climb and you have wood and the required building tools, keep moving to create distance while selecting a foundation. Place it ahead of you where building is allowed, then quickly jump onto it. This only helps if placement succeeds, you can reach the top and it is high enough. If placement fails, do not stand still repeatedly trying.

Keep some wood with you

When exploring, carry enough wood for a foundation and practice switching to your building tool, selecting the foundation and jumping. Wood is useful for everyday building and can also help you create a temporary refuge during a chase.

gather-resources-quickly.title: How to gather resources quickly
gather-resources-quickly.html:
Combine cloth gathering, roadside sign collection and recycling spare items to build up useful resources as you explore.

More ways to get cloth

Collect harvestable cloth when you find it in the wilderness. In the desert, you can also harvest cacti for cloth, but watch out for cactus damage and keep an eye on your health.

Use an axe or machete to chop the bodies of dead animals or NPCs and obtain cloth. The amount may vary between bodies.

Recycle spare items into cloth

Recyclers offer another source of cloth. Sewing kits, tarps and rope have cloth among their recycling outputs. Recycle spares, check the outputs first and keep equipment you still need.

Collect signs along the road

While exploring roads, hit roadside signs to collect Road Signs items, then take them to a recycler. This lets you gather recyclable resources along your route.

The site’s current item table lists scrap as the recycling output for Road Signs. Scrap and metal fragments are different items, so this guide does not present signs as a confirmed source of metal fragments.

Tip: shoot barrels and road signs with a crossbow

Carry a crossbow and some bolts. Shooting metal barrels and road signs is a quick way to gather resources without repeatedly swinging a melee tool, saving that tool’s durability.

Make each trip count

Gather cloth when you see it, look for cacti in the desert, harvest animal or NPC bodies when safe, and collect signs along roads. Recycle suitable spare items when you return to a recycler.

scrap-road-loop.title: Collect scrap along the road, then return home
scrap-road-loop.text: Check your tools’ durability before leaving and bring spare tools and basic supplies. Link nearby roads, town outskirts and barrel areas into a loop. Return home to store your haul after one circuit instead of continuing farther and farther. If an area has already been looted, move to the next stretch rather than waiting there. End the trip when your tools are nearly broken or you have collected plenty of scrap. Your haul depends on the route and other players, so do not chase a fixed hourly yield.

weapon-choice-by-trip.title: Choose weapons for the trip
weapon-choice-by-trip.text: Before equipping yourself, decide whether you are gathering, fighting at close range or exploring a dangerous area. For everyday gathering, you can pair a melee weapon with a reliable ranged weapon. Indoor encounters call for close-range handling, while fights in open areas require attention to range. Before unlocking a new gun, budget for both crafting materials and future ammunition. Research weapons you use often and can keep supplied with ammo; you do not need to unlock every gun at once. Even after getting more expensive equipment, keep an affordable everyday loadout.

battle-pass-mission-route.title: Check Battle Pass missions before planning your route
battle-pass-mission-route.text: Check daily missions when you log in and fit objectives such as opening crates and mining into your planned route. Click Claim after completing a mission; watching the progress bar is not enough. Daily missions are replaced the next day, and unfinished ones do not carry over. Spread longer weekly missions over several sessions. You can still complete earlier weeks’ objectives before the season ends; some missions require the Elite Pass. Near the end of the season, check the time remaining and unfinished objectives before deciding which missions to focus on.

base-location-checklist.title: Check four things before choosing a base site
base-location-checklist.html:
Before spending all your materials on a large base, walk around the site. Check whether it is visible from a busy road, whether wood, stone and metal are nearby, whether you have a practical route home with loot, and whether there is room for more doors, storage or another floor.

If the site cannot offer everything, a solo player can first prioritize a small, lockable shelter and a return route they know well. A resource-rich spot is not automatically worth building beside a busy path. Place a Tool Cupboard, door, respawn point and a little storage, then watch local player traffic over several gathering trips before expanding.

This is a way to compare locations, not a promise that any terrain is safe. Map layout, server population and nearby players change the risk. Do not copy coordinates from someone else’s video without checking the site yourself.

starter-core-expansion.title: Secure a small core before expanding to a 2×2 base
starter-core-expansion.html:
Build in two stages. First bring enough materials to close and lock a small core with a Tool Cupboard, door, basic storage and respawn point. Store your first gathering haul there. Later, when you know what materials and nearby player activity allow, expand toward a full 2×2 layout, add rooms and strengthen the outer walls.

This order reduces the time you stand in the open holding building materials. Before expanding, use the placement preview to check door swing, internal walkways and the Tool Cupboard position. Filling the core with boxes too early may leave no room for a door or stairs. In a team, agree who brings doors and upkeep materials.

A creator’s “five-minute build” depends on practice, supplies and server conditions. The useful idea is to secure the core first and expand afterward; the time claim is not a guarantee.

two-door-entry.title: Use two doors to reduce exposure at the entrance
two-door-entry.html:
Leave a small space between two entrance doors. When leaving, close the inner door before opening the outer one. When returning, close the outer door before opening the inner one or sorting your backpack. This makes it harder for someone watching the entrance to see straight into the storage core during one door opening.

Walk through the finished entrance yourself. Check that the doors do not block each other, that you can close them while being chased, and that carried items do not trap you. Keep locks, doors and storage from forming one exposed line. More doors also slow you and your teammates down, so match the entrance to the size of your group.

A two-door entrance reduces one kind of exposure; it does not make a base raid-proof. Confirm the exact layout with the in-game building preview.

compact-base-storage.title: Organize storage before stacking boxes in a compact base
compact-base-storage.html:
A small base does not always need a bigger footprint. Separate everyday materials, weapons and ammunition, and backup supplies. Try placing boxes along walls first. If floor space is tight, test whether half-walls, shelves or another level can safely add storage without blocking access.

Leave space to open doors, turn around, reach the furnace and open every box. Put frequently used supplies near the entrance while keeping valuable items away from the first door. A box that fits but cannot be opened, or blocks a building or repair point, does not improve the base. Test a layout in Sandbox or with cheap materials first.

An outside example fits twelve large boxes into one specific mini base. That count is not a promise that the same layout works in every version or room.

window-exit-scouting.title: Use observation windows to check outside before opening a door
window-exit-scouting.html:
If you add an observation window, place it where it can show your usual entrance and nearby hiding spots. Before leaving with valuable supplies, look at the door area and both sides. If you hear footsteps or gunfire outside, identify the position before stepping out.

Test the view in game. Seeing the doorway does not mean you can shoot safely from inside, and outside players may also see you. Make sure you can retreat, close a door, change angle or alert teammates after spotting a threat. Move a window if it exposes the storage core.

The aim is to gather information before opening the door. A particular number of metal windows does not guarantee a successful defense.

respawn-point-layout.title: Separate respawn points instead of clustering them in one room
respawn-point-layout.html:
If your server allows several usable beds or sleeping bags, give them different jobs. One can be near protected backup equipment in the core; another can be nearer a safer exit for checking the situation outside. Keep a usable path between them. Avoid spawning directly in front of intruders or into blocked furniture.

Before relying on this layout, verify that each point can actually be selected and that you can use the nearby locks and supplies after respawning. If only one point is available, put it where you can recover safely and reach backup gear. Extra points are not worth blocking essential storage or movement.

A three-bed base shown by a creator is one design, not evidence that every server has the same placement limit, cooldown or respawn rules. Test those rules on your own server.

door-path-retreat.title: Plan your own retreat when adding more doors
door-path-retreat.html:
Extra doors can slow intruders, but they also slow you. Trace your normal route from the outer door to the Tool Cupboard, storage and respawn point. Then trace a route back to a safer room while being chased. If both routes bottleneck at the same door or corner, change the layout before adding another door.

Walk the route with your usual gear and ask teammates to enter and leave as well. Check for doors that block each other, a teammate being locked on the dangerous side, and whether medicine and ammunition remain quick to reach. Keep daily supplies accessible and valuable items deeper inside.

Long door paths appear in player build examples, but more doors are not automatically better value. Consider material cost, upkeep and everyday access on your own server.

nighttime-preparation.title: Use nighttime to organize and prepare for the next trip
nighttime-preparation.html:
If night falls while you are in an unfamiliar area, consider staying near base. Sort materials, restock the Tool Cupboard, craft tools and ammunition for the next trip, and choose a daylight destination on the map. This avoids testing an unfamiliar route with valuable loot when visibility is poor.

If you must travel at night, decide on the destination and a reason to turn back. Bring enough food, water, lighting or defensive gear and leave room to retreat through dangerous areas. A route you used by day may still be risky at night, especially on a busy server.

This is a way to reduce uncertainty. It does not claim that night causes extra damage or follows a fixed loot schedule. Other players may also use darkness to stay hidden.

return-with-valuable-loot.title: Decide when to return before your backpack fills with valuables
return-with-valuable-loot.html:
Set a return trigger before leaving: you have the target materials, are nearly out of medicine, your tool is close to breaking, or you now carry components you do not want to lose. Once that trigger is reached, plan the trip home instead of extending the run for one more container.

On the way back, look for cover, likely enemy positions and alternate routes. A fight with a passerby may be less valuable than safely banking rare components. If spotted, decide whether you can disengage before firing. Unload promptly at home and carry only what you need on the next trip.

There is no universal backpack-slot threshold. The value of returning depends on your loot, distance, server activity and team support.

new-gun-total-cost.title: Count research, crafting and ammunition before switching guns
new-gun-total-cost.html:
Do not judge a new gun only by its crafting recipe. Check its prerequisite nodes and Scrap research cost, then the weapon components, then whether you have enough ammunition, gunpowder and metal to take it into the field. A gun that you can craft but cannot keep supplied may be less useful for now than one you already know.

Make a three-column checklist: unlock, craft and resupply. Choose a near-term purpose—hunting, exploring or player combat—before choosing a research path. There is no universal best weapon order. Use this site’s recipe and weapon pages to check current client materials, then confirm what your server actually allows.

This guide focuses on the cost of continuing to use a weapon. It does not adopt damage rankings from outside articles that lack comparable test conditions or may describe an older version.
